## Usage

```{r setup}
library(damR)
exdata_path <- list.files(
  system.file(package = "damR", "extdata"),
  "example_data.csv",
  full.names = TRUE
)
```


## Load and clean data

`ReadFile()` expects a wide-format dataset where the rows are samples and
columns are metabolites.

```{r}
read.csv(exdata_path)[1:10, 1:5]
```

The `Sample` column should be in the form
`SampleID_Subgroup1ID-Subgroup2ID_BatchNo` to infer Sample, Group, Subgroup, and
Batch identifiers based on the "_" and "-" delimiters. The Metabolite column
must be in the form `MetaboliteName_ExtractionMethod` for filtering based on
extraction method (IP/HILIC/T3Acidic).

```{r}
(mdata <- ReadFile(exdata_path))
```

`ReadFile()` pivots the data from wide to long or tidy form for the rest of the
analysis.

## QC

Each metabolite in the dataset may be sampled with multiple extraction methods.
For each metabolite, `FilterExtraction()` selects the method with the fewest NAs
or the lowest variation. `FilterBlanks()` runs blank filtering to remove
metabolites from non-blank samples that fail to meet a specified fold-change
threshold compared to the same metabolites from blank samples. To identify the
data that get blank filtered without running the filtering, use
`GetBlankDropTable()` which `FilterBlanks()` uses to identify the metabolites to
remove as well as the blank samples.

`QCData` is a top-level function that calls both `FilterExtraction()` and
`FilterBlanks()`, and removes metabolites with low variance. 

```{r}
to_drop <- GetBlankDropTable(mdata)
head(to_drop$dropTable)
to_drop$blanks

qc_data <- QCData(mdata)
```

`RemoveMissing()` drops metabolites with more NAs than a specified proportion.
To identify those that would be removed without removing them, call
`IdentifyMissing()`. Run `PlotMissingness()` to get a presence/absence heatmap
of your data.

```{r}
PlotMissingness(qc_data)
head(IdentifyMissing(qc_data))
rm_data <- RemoveMissing(qc_data)
```

To examine your data before and after QC, you can use PCA. By default it returns
a `ggplot` object but if `ggiraph` is available, setting `interactive = TRUE`
and using `ggiraph::girafe()` to render the plot will produce an interactive
plot.

```{r fig.height = 10}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
ggiraph_available <- requireNamespace("ggiraph", quietly = TRUE)

pca.raw <- PlotPCA(GetPCA(mdata), interactive = ggiraph_available) + ggtitle("Raw")
pca.qc <- PlotPCA(GetPCA(qc_data), interactive = ggiraph_available) + ggtitle("QC")
pca.rm <- PlotPCA(GetPCA(rm_data), interactive = ggiraph_available) +
  ggtitle("Missingness removed")

pcas <- list(pca.raw, pca.qc, pca.rm) |> wrap_plots(nrow = 3, guides = "collect")

if (ggiraph_available) ggiraph::girafe(pcas) else pcas
```



## Imputation

```{r}
imputed_data <- impute.QRILC(rm_data)
```

## Model fitting

`DiffMetabolites()` uses `limma` to compute differential abundance of
metabolites on specified groups. If unspecified, all unique Group identifiers
are compared. By default, it produce contrasts in both directions for to make
comparisons easy to view and plot: with groups A, B, and C the contrasts are A -
B, A - C, and B - C as well as B - A, C - A, and C - B. Set `reverseContrasts =
FALSE` if you want just one direction.

```{r}
groups <- unique(imputed_data$Group)

results <- DiffMetabolites(imputed_data)

PlotVolcano(results, groups[c(1, 5)], contrastTitle = "Example", cap = 5)
```

As with the PCA plots, setting `interactive = TRUE` produces interactive volcano
plots.  With `PlotAllVolcanoes()` you can plot multiple groups, returned as a
lit of plots. Here we collect the captions that show up when the fold-changes
are capped and the common main title into a single title and caption.


```{r fig.width = 6}
all_volcanoes.list <- PlotAllVolcanoes(
  results,
  groups[c(1:3)],
  cap = 10,
  contrastTitle = "Example",
  interactive = ggiraph_available
)

# extract the caption to 'collect' it
caption <- all_volcanoes.list[[1]]@labels$caption
title <- all_volcanoes.list[[1]]@labels$title

# drop the titles and captions
all_volcanoes <- lapply(all_volcanoes.list, \(p) p + labs(title = NULL, caption = NULL)) |>
  wrap_plots(guides = "collect") &
  theme_minimal(7) &
  theme(legend.position = "top") &
  plot_annotation(title = title, caption = caption)

if (ggiraph_available) ggiraph::girafe(all_volcanoes) else all_volcanoes
```

## Heatmap of significantly differentially abundant metabolites

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=8}
PlotSigMetabolites(
  results,
  imputed_data,
  color = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "Greys"),
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  show_rownames = FALSE
)
```



## Pipeline

```r
fc_data <- ReadFile(exdata_path) |>
  QCData() |>
  RemoveMissing() |>
  impute.QRILC() |>
  DiffMetabolites()
```
